decisions.reason: As a multi-variant decoration fabric line close to the core assortment, it fits the firm's stocked-service model and management can justify keeping it by pointing to sunk collection and sampling costs and possible temporary market weakness.

This transparent burnout decorative fabric is a visible but still closely related extension of the existing decorative range, so the firm is likely to persist rather than admit an early withdrawal after a public launch.

Because it overlaps with the established decorative fabric business but seems narrower than the larger lines, it is somewhat more exposed to pruning, yet escalation of commitment still makes continued offering more likely than removal.

The velour-like upholstery fabric builds directly on the firm's upholstery offer and warehouse-based continuity promise, giving management both strategic and psychological reasons to keep it in the range.

The flame-retardant inbetween fabric supports a practical customer need within the firm's established market, so management is likely to defend the launch and attribute any weak uptake to temporary conditions rather than product failure.

Although this polyester lining fabric is a more standard supporting product and therefore somewhat easier to cut, it still complements the core textile assortment and prior launch commitment makes near-term withdrawal less likely.
